newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower as markets test RB tolerance.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower as markets test RB tolerance.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended half a U.S. cent lower on Friday as markets presumed Reserve Bank acceptance of easier monetary conditions.
The kiwi closed at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6446/53 compared with its 0.6497/04 opening while the Trade-Weighted Index ended at 64.39 from 64.78.
The Monetary Conditions Index eased to 740, some 85 basis points easier than the Reserve Bank's desired level and 35 basis points beyond the tolerance limit it has set out as acceptable.
"I don't think the bank will be particularly concerned," said one dealer.
"The general perception is they will let conditions ease just a little bit. If we get to 100 points or more (diversion on the MCI) there will be big problems."
He said the bank would not want to see variable mortgage rates any higher than their typical 10.4 percent level with the economy and confidence at weak levels.
"They may allow the currency and conditions to be a little easier than they normally would like," he added.
Dealers said the two-for-one trade-off in monetary conditions between the currency and interest rates used by the bank in its MCI formula seemed less applicable at present.

The next key for New Zealand financial markets is expected to be Tuesday's jobs data which should give a strong indication of whether the economy is weaker than the RBNZ has forecast -- as private sector economists suggest.
Meanwhile, the weak Australian dollar continued to exert downward pressure on the kiwi.
Dealers said option plays had made the market long and traders were unloading risk.
The kiwi traded in a 0.6435-0.6503 range. The 0.6440-50 area held reasonably well through the session, however, and dealers said there were plenty of buyers around that level.
"It's still looking reasonably good at this sort of level here," said one.
However, some dealers see the kiwi heading down to 0.6380 early next week before it finds more solid support.
